assistant|saffron_syrup_recipe: Saffron-infused simple syrup uses 1 cup sugar, 1 cup water, 1/2 teaspoon saffron threads (about 10-12 threads)

assistant|saffron_storage: Saffron threads should be stored in an airtight container in a dark, cool (60-70°F), dry place away from heat
assistant|saffron_shelf_life: High-quality saffron lasts 2-3 years, medium-quality 1-2 years, low-quality a few months to a year when stored properly
assistant|saffron_freezing: Saffron threads can be frozen in an airtight container at 0°F or below and last up to 5 years

assistant|saffron_quantity_4x: For a quadruple batch (4 cups syrup), 40-45 saffron threads (2-2.25 teaspoons) are needed
assistant|saffron_retailers: Recommended sources for high-quality saffron: Penzeys Spices, The Spice House, Amazon, Middle Eastern/Indian grocery stores, and specialty food stores
assistant|saffron_price_range: High-quality saffron ranges from $5 to $15 per gram depending on quality and origin
assistant|saffron_origin_quality: Saffron from La Mancha (Spain), Kashmir (India), and Iran is considered high quality
assistant|naan_flour_tip: Naan bread traditionally uses atta (chapati) flour, a finely milled whole wheat flour; all-purpose flour can be substituted

assistant|saffron_yield: A good quality saffron thread yields about 3-4 times its weight in flavor and color
